newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech NPF delays Vitkovice steel selloff.
newsitem.headline: Czech NPF delays Vitkovice steel selloff.

text.p: The Czech privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), said on Tuesday it would delay the cabinet-approved sale of a 20 percent stake in steel mill Vitkovice a.s. at least until 1998.
NPF spokesman Milos Ruzicka said poor Vitkovice earnings results and lengthy recession on the steel products markets were the reasons for the delay.
He said the other part of the plan, the sale of a 20 percent stake in another steel mill, Nova Hut a.s., on the capital market would go ahead as planned.

"It is just a delay of the sale of Vitkovice. The plan still stands, we just decided to split the sale of the two companies," said Ruzicka. "We know... we would get a lot for one of the firms and little for the other one."
He said separating the sale should bring better revenue prospects for the fund.
Vitkovice lost 765 million crowns ($26.2 million) last year, after a 352 million net profit in 1995.

Under a partial management buy-out plan, one percent stakes in both Vitkovice and Nova Hut have been sold to their managements, along with an option for another 10 to 15 percent once restructuring plans set by the government are fulfiled.
-- Pavel Novak, Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003 ($ = 29.20 Czech Crowns)
